title: Pagan Empire
summary: Pagan, on a bend of the Irrawaddy, was the capital of the first great Burmese state. Its first historical king, Anawrahta (1044-1077), consolidated central Burma by conquering the Pyu and the Mon; after taking Buddhist texts from the Mon state of Thaton he made Theravada Buddhism the state religion. Kings built thousands of temples, stupas and monasteries, and 3,595 monuments are recorded today. Pagan's art set models copied by later kingdoms. In 1287, as the Mongols threatened, King Narathihapati fled the capital.

uncertainty.note: Traditional founding dated to the accession of King Anawrahta in 1044; the empire collapsed following the Mongol invasions of 1287.
